title: Martin takes first DTM win from pole in Moscow
dek: Maxime Martin turned his first DTM pole into his first win at Moscow Raceway, finishing 4.259 seconds clear of fellow BMW driver Bruno Spengler after two safety cars and an Audi collision.

chapters.title: Wittmann leads as the field reaches Russia
text: The fifth round of the ten-race 2014 DTM season was held at Moscow Raceway on Sunday 13 July, and it began with Marco Wittmann at the head of the drivers’ table on 58 points. Edoardo Mortara was second on 39, with Mattias Ekström and Mike Rockenfeller level on 35 behind him. Wittmann had already won the opening race at Hockenheim and the third round at the Hungaroring, while the Norisring a fortnight earlier had gone to Mercedes-Benz’s Robert Wickens, who won from pole.

The race was set for 46 laps of the 3.931-kilometre circuit on the outskirts of the Russian capital, with the usual mandatory pit stop and a choice between the softer Hankook option tyre and the harder prime. Which compound to start on, and how the stops would fall, were the main strategic questions of the weekend.

Rookies set much of the tone. Nico Müller, in only his fifth DTM race for Audi, was quickest in free practice, and Maxime Martin arrived at BMW Team RMG for his fifth race weekend in the series without a pole position to his name. Mercedes, by contrast, came to Russia with its recent winner but little pace.

chapters.title: Martin beats Spengler to a first pole
text: Martin comfortably cleared the first of the three knockout segments in fifth place, then topped the second with 1:28.523, the quickest lap of the weekend to that point. The final segment was a scramble. Rockenfeller set the early mark at 1:28.813, Bruno Spengler, who had only just scraped through in seventh, jumped to the top with 1:28.638, and Martin answered about a minute from the end with 1:28.619 to take the first pole of his DTM career by 0.019 seconds.

Müller was third in the Rosberg Audi, 0.095 seconds off the pole time, and called it a good day after the Swiss had topped free practice. Rockenfeller took fourth on the same time as the Swiss driver, with Adrien Tambay fifth, Augusto Farfus sixth, championship leader Wittmann seventh and Miguel Molina eighth. Jamie Green and Timo Glock completed the top ten. Ekström, strong in practice, could manage only 11th, and Mortara was 12th.

It was a poor day for Mercedes. Wickens, the Norisring winner, was the best of them in 14th, while Pascal Wehrlein, Gary Paffett, Christian Vietoris and Vitaly Petrov filled four of the last five places on the time sheet. Petrov, the only Russian in the field, ended up on the back row in 23rd, and Martin Tomczyk lined up 22nd in his BMW.

chapters.title: A crowded start and a soft-tyre gamble
text: Martin led from the start and was never seriously challenged. Behind him it was busy. Wittmann said afterwards that he was under fire in the opening phase and that his priority was to come through in one piece, while Glock moved up to run as high as third. Green’s race was over on lap 6, and Paul di Resta was out two laps later.

A group of drivers had gone against the grain on tyres. Farfus, António Félix da Costa and Molina started on the softer Hankook option, and Spengler, who also began on the options, said he lost a little time in that first stint. A late-race advantage for the soft-tyre group was expected, and with a clear track it was put at around two seconds a lap.

chapters.title: Two neutralisations and an Audi collision
text: That clean run never came. On lap 23 Timo Scheider’s Audi stopped on the pit straight and the safety car stayed out until lap 28. On the restart Rockenfeller, who was due to pit a lap later, locked his front tyres behind Tambay and slid into the back of the Abt Audi. Both cars were out on the spot and the safety car came out again. Rockenfeller, the reigning champion, took the blame, saying he was incredibly sorry and that his front wheels perhaps had not been warm enough, while Tambay refused to point a finger and said he believed a podium had been on.

The neutralisations also erased Martin’s lead and wrecked the softer-tyre plan. Farfus said the long safety car phases left him on the standard tyres for much longer than intended, and Félix da Costa said too many laps had been lost behind the safety car for his strategy to matter. Farfus eventually finished 10th, Félix da Costa 11th and Molina 12th.

chapters.title: Martin wins by 4.259 seconds
text: Martin took the flag after 46 laps in 1:15:09.422, 4.259 seconds ahead of Spengler, giving BMW a one-two in Russia. Behind them Ekström staged the recovery of the day, climbing from 11th on the grid to third, 9.454 seconds from the winner, and he was one of three drivers, with Wittmann and Müller, to pass Glock on lap 44.

Glock had been on course for a podium but said he lost fuel pressure after the safety car and dropped to sixth. Wittmann took fourth, only a little over a tenth behind Ekström, and Müller was fifth. Vietoris was seventh and Wehrlein eighth for Mercedes, Mortara ninth and Farfus tenth. Molina set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:28.305 on lap 37. Petrov, in front of his home crowd, was the last classified finisher in 18th, while Rockenfeller, Tambay, Scheider, Di Resta and Green were all out.

chapters.title: Wittmann stretches his lead to 20 points
text: Martin called his first win “simply incredible” and said a DTM seat had always been his dream. He thanked BMW Team RMG for what he described as an awesome pit stop and spot-on strategy. It was the third victory in five races for the Reinhold-led RMG squad after Wittmann’s two earlier wins, and BMW Motorsport Director Jens Marquardt called Martin simply unbeatable all weekend and the result the most successful of the season so far.

Spengler congratulated the winner, said he had struggled on the options in the first stint and found much more pace once on the primes, and described the one-two as a dream result for BMW. Wittmann was happy to have survived the start phase and extended his lead with fourth. Glock was left to rue what might have been: he said BMW had been within touching distance of a one-two-three before his fuel pressure dropped.

For Audi it was a costly day. Rockenfeller, who had gone into the weekend level on 35 points with Ekström, scored nothing and stayed on 35, while Ekström’s podium moved him to 50 points and second in the table. Mercedes’ best result was seventh for Vietoris. Wickens, the Norisring winner, finished 14th after qualifying 14th, and Paul di Resta’s race ended on lap 8. Müller’s fifth place, from third on the grid, rewarded an Audi rookie who had set the pace in practice, but Audi’s afternoon was defined by the two cars lost in one corner. Tambay said the pair had lost a podium and that two Audis colliding was something that should not happen.

After five of the ten races Wittmann leads on 70 points, 20 clear of Ekström, with Spengler and Mortara tied on 41, Rockenfeller on 35 and Martin, the newest winner, up to sixth on 33. The championship moves to the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg on 3 August, with five races remaining.

facts.v: Maxime Martin won from pole by 4.259 seconds over Bruno Spengler in the fifth DTM race weekend of his career, taking the flag after 46 laps in 1:15:09.422.
